item.title: 10 Best Black Friday Board Game Deals
item.dc:creator: Corey Plante
item.description: [Filtered: Generic shopping list; no specific game news or analysis.] The best Black Friday 2026 deals on board games for casual and hardcore players alike.
item.content:encoded: One of the great joys of the holidays is finally getting everyone around the same table. Another is watching your cousin realize that the road they’ve been building for the last six turns is about to go nowhere. You don’t get many chances to do that as an adult. Make the most of it.

item.title: Illumination Takes Over Macy’s Parade With New Not Alone Thanksgiving Teaser
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: [Filtered: Animated movie promo; lacks substance for keep threshold.] Illumination gives a better look at Not Alone in a new teaser where the three hectic aliens crash a Thanksgiving parade.
item.content:encoded: There's no doubt that 2026 has been a great year for Illumination. It had one of the biggest releases of the year with The Super Mario Galaxy Movie in April, earning over $1 billion. Then, in June, it released another hit Minion movie, Minions & Monsters, which made $531 million. It's no surprise that fans were looking forward to more from the animation company.

item.title: 5 Years Later, an Avengers: Doomsday Hero's Next MCU Adventure Is Finally Moving Forward
item.dc:creator: Francesco Cacciatore
item.description: [Filtered: Big-franchise Marvel churn; Avengers casting/production gossip.] Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings' writer Dave Callaham says he's working on the sequel's screenplay, and there is 'some real movement.'
item.content:encoded: Shang-Chi is getting ready to return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe in Avengers: Doomsday, but fans hoping to see more of the hero have another reason to be optimistic. Dave Callaham, who co-wrote Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, has confirmed that he's working on a sequel, offering the clearest sign yet that the character's next solo adventure is moving forward.

item.title: 10 Best Black Friday 2026 Book Deals For Sci-Fi and Fantasy Fans
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Generic book shopping list; not gaming or horror focused.] Give the gift of a genre classic or a brand new novel
item.content:encoded: Books make a perfect gift. They offer the chance to introduce a friend or family member to a story or world you love and adventures you can share together. You can even use a book as a seed for future gift ideas by getting someone hooked on a series. Black Friday sales offer plenty of bargains on fantasy and sci-fi classics and recent genre standouts for anyone looking to get an early start on holiday shopping. Even if you’re just looking for some reading material for your vacation, you should check out the 10 best Black Friday book deals.

item.title: 8 Essential Thriller Books Everyone Should Read at Least Once
item.dc:creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
item.description: [Filtered: Generic book listicle; outside core interests.] These must-read genre books offer a lot more than a thrilling distraction from reality.
item.content:encoded: Take genre staples like Gone Girl or The Silent Patient. While the two couldn’t be more different in tone and subject matter, both thrillers heavily rely on misdirection and the recontextualization of events to deliver twists. These picks are a staple in every “must-read” list for good reason, just like the ones Polygon has highlighted below as genre essentials. Without further ado, here are eight thriller books you should read at least once in your life.

item.title: 8 Funniest ‘Far Side’ Comics About Fruits and Vegetables
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip, not gaming or core interests.] Gary Larson’s comic strip The Far Side featured jokes about all kinds of things, including fruits and vegetables. Here are the 8 funniest.
item.content:encoded: Decades after Gary Larson concluded his comic strip The Far Side back in 1995, fans of the series continue to read it regularly, and new fans are discovering it all the time. Some of Larson’s most beloved comic strips feature animals drawn in his signature style, including dogs, chickens, and especially cows. He often gave these animals human-like intelligence and other anthropomorphic traits and depicted them in very human-like scenarios.

item.title: 32 Years Later, Disney's Most Notorious Cash-Grab Sequel Is Better Than You Remember
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old Disney sequel.] The Aladdin sequel The Return of Jafar is often derided as a bad, cheap sequel which started Disney's direct-to-video sequel trend, but I love it
item.content:encoded: Ever since former Disney CEO Bob Chapek released his autobiography last September, a rather unexpected Disney movie has been a topic for discussion: the direct-to-VHS sequel to Aladdintitled The Return of Jafar. Released in 1994, The Return of Jafar was the first in a long line of direct-to-VHS (and later direct-to-DVD) sequels to theatrical Disney films. Besides Aladdin, Disney made sequels to The Lion King, The Little Mermaid, Pocahontas, Mulan, and several other then-modern Disney animated features, as well as some much older classics like Cinderella and Bambi. These movies used cheaper animation produced by Disney’s TV division and were developed in far less time than Disney spends developing animated feature films.

item.title: 7 Years Later, Hollywood’s Most Notorious Fantasy Flop Deserves Another Shot
item.dc:creator: Corey Plante
item.description: [Filtered: Years-later retrospective of old movie, no substance.] Seven years later, a first watch of Tom Hooper’s Cats on Netflix finds plenty to enjoy, especially Taylor Swift’s catnip number.
item.content:encoded: I vividly remember learning the phrase “uncanny valley” in 2019. First came the trailer for Sonic the Hedgehog that April, with those alarmingly human teeth. Then came the first trailer for Tom Hooper’s Cats in July. Suddenly, there was a name for a feeling I’d had my whole life. The uncanny valley is that uneasy feeling you get when something looks or moves almost like a real person, but some small detail makes the whole thing feel wrong. That feeling is a lot more common these days, now that AI-generated videos are everywhere. But it was Cats that really brought the uncanny valley into the popular lexicon.

item.title: The 14 Best Star Wars Games of All Time, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Jason Venter
item.description: [Filtered: Star Wars big-franchise churn list piece.] Out of the many Star Wars games released over the years, these fantastic titles deserve your attention now and forever.
item.content:encoded: Star Wars video games date all the way back to The Empire Strikes Back on the Atari 2600 in 1982. Since then, the franchise itself has largely matured alongside the medium, encompassing everything from role-playing games and first-person shooters to arcade racers and XCOM clones (the latter of two seeing well-regard releases just this year). No matter the year or the hardware, some of the best Star Wars games are worth revisiting. Here are the 12 best Star Wars games of all time, ranked.

item.title: Prime Video Is Saying Goodbye to Six Decades of James Bond Movies
item.dc:creator: Sam Hill
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming content leaving service, clickbait pattern.] Nearly every James Bond movie is leaving Prime Video on Nov. 30, including Casino Royale, GoldenEye, Skyfall, and No Time to Die.
item.content:encoded: James Bond fans looking to revisit the legendary spy's cinematic adventures might want to clear their schedules before the end of November. Prime Video is preparing to remove a huge chunk of the 007 franchise from its streaming library, with nearly every James Bond movie currently available on the platform scheduled to leave at the same time.

item.title: 'Alien' Meets 'Vikings' in a 2008 Sci-Fi Spin on Beowulf That Deserves Redemption
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about 2008 sci-fi film, not game-related.] A space marine learns to love Norse drinking games
item.content:encoded: Beowulf is one of the oldest surviving pieces of English literature, and its story of a hero defending the Danes from a monster has inspired numerous adaptations. John McTiernan told the story in his 1999 film The 13th Warrior, and Robert Zemeckis used motion capture for a 2007 version. But my favorite telling of the story eschews history and fantasy to turn the tale of Beowulf and Grendel into an Alien-inspired sci-fi action flick.

item.title: 51 Years Later, One of Peanuts’ Best Sally Brown Strips Is Still a Perfect School Joke
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Comic strip retrospective, not gaming or Polygon core content.] In a 1975 Peanuts strip, Sally Brown turns a tip from Linus about rock snakes into one of her funniest school reports.
item.content:encoded: For years, one of the problems with reading Charles Schulz's Peanuts was the inconsistency among its collected editions. You'd think that Peanuts’ publishers, as the stewards of one of the most influential comic strips in the Western world, would simply reprint the comics in chronological order. It was rarely that simple.

item.title: The Lord of the Rings’ Next Movie Officially Wraps Production, but Now the Hard Part Begins
item.dc:creator: Francesco Cacciatore
item.category: The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum
item.description: [Filtered: Film production news without notable substance or prestige anchor.] Will Andy Serkis' 'The Hunt for Gollum' be able to revitalize the franchise more than a decade after The Hobbit trilogy?
item.content:encoded: Warner Bros. announced on Nov. 25, 2026, that production on the next installment in The Lord of the Rings movie franchise has wrapped. The Hunt for Gollum, directed by Andy Serkis, is currently headed for post-production ahead of the movie's Dec. 17, 2027 release. The news follows Serkis' announcement in November that filming had ended.

item.title: 20 Years Later, One of TV’s Greatest Sci-Fi Franchises Still Hasn’t Topped Its Riskiest Spin-Off
item.dc:creator: Aimee Hart
item.description: [Filtered: TV retrospective, not horror, prestige, or genuinely anticipated project.] Russell T. Davies did an amazing job on 'The War Between Land and Sea,' but if you ask us, it's still no 'Torchwood.'
item.content:encoded: Last year was a mixed bag for Whovians. Disney dumped Doctor Who, leaving the franchise in such dire straits that the BBC had no choice but to look for someone new to steer the long-running sci-fi show into a new era. That said, the franchise also got a major win with Russell T. Davies and director Dylan Holmes-Williams’s climate-focused spin-off, The War Between Land and Sea, which debuted in the U.K. that December but still hasn't officially been released in the U.S.

item.title: 10 Classic Books Worth Reading Over and Over
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Generic book list, outside gaming and core Polygon interests.] From Russian masterpieces to modern dystopias, these are the books that never get old.
item.content:encoded: Most of us treat classic literature like a checklist to conquer in high school or college and then never touch those books again. You power through the plot, underline a few quotes for a term paper, and move on to whatever else is new. The catch is that great books rarely reveal their most fascinating tricks on the first pass. When you already know the ending, your brain stops racing for answers and begins to notice the machinery holding all those mysteries and themes together. Suddenly, an unreliable narrator's sleight of hand becomes obvious, or a throwaway line in chapter two hits like a freight train in light of later developments.

item.title: 6 Fantasy Books Better Than Harry Potter
item.dc:creator: S.W. Sondheimer
item.description: [Filtered: Book recommendations list, not gaming or adjacent Polygon content.] Great fantasy books like Darker by Four, Impossible Creatures, and Six of Crows are arguably even better than Harry Potter.
item.content:encoded: There's no denying that Harry Potter continues to be a phenomenon. After seven bestsellers translated into multiple languages, years of extravagant midnight release parties, eight big-budget films, a stage play, and theme parks, there's still enormous hype for both the upcoming HBO television show and an all-star re-recording of the audiobooks. Clearly, there is something about the boy who lived and his world that draws people in and keeps them captivated. All of this begs one very important question, however: how good are the Harry Potter books, really?

item.title: How to get adrenaline in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] You can get more adrenaline in GTA 6 by looking in specific places at robbery locations or in ambulances. Here's how to get adrenaline in GTA 6
item.content:encoded: Adrenaline acts as an emergency boost to all your stats in Grand Theft Auto 6, as it temporarily negates health, stamina, and focus loss. It's meant to get you out of an emergency situation safely or help you burst into a tense situation and mop it up fast. Unlike Zombix and other restoratives, though, you can't buy adrenaline — not from anywhere we've found so far, at least — nor can you expect to find it in abundance throughout Leonida. There is, however, a small set of locations you can reliably get adrenaline from.

item.title: All Peewees Billboard locations in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Johnny Yu
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Peewees Billboards will lead you to a grand prize in GTA 6. Here's where you can find them all, how to solve the puzzle, and how to claim the reward.
item.content:encoded: Peewees Billboards are one of the many scannable WAiNK collectibles in Grand Theft Auto 6, but they're also part of the Mr. Enigma X Peewees scavenger hunt. Mr. Enigma, a play on Dr. Pepper, and the Peewees, a play on Popeyes, have teamed up to create a challenge where you must find four Peewees billboards, and you'll earn a valuable reward.

item.title: 'Avengers: Doomsday' Is Making Sure Patrick Stewart Gets a Proper Sendoff
item.dc:creator: Sam Hill
item.description: [Filtered: Marvel franchise casting/set gossip; big-franchise churn.] Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige confirms a Patrick Stewart tribute is being planned for Avengers: Doomsday.
item.content:encoded: Patrick Stewart's final on-screen performance will arrive in December's Avengers: Doomsday, and Marvel is making sure the late actor receives a fitting farewell.

item.title: All Key Lento standout vehicles in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Ford James
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Standout vehicles are one of the many collectibles in GTA 6. Here's where to find every one in Key Lento.
item.content:encoded: There are 12 standout vehicles in Key Lento in Grand Theft Auto 6, ranging from an incredibly festive boat to a pizza delivery car, and finding them all is essential if you want to 100% complete the game. GTA 6 has 280 standout vehicles to find in total, and some of them are very tough to find, so we're here to help.

item.title: How to whistle to distract enemies in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Paulo Kawanishi
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's how to whistle in GTA 6 and when you can whistle, one of the best skills to use if you plan on hiding from enemies and taking them by surprise.
item.content:encoded: Knowing how to whistle in Grand Theft Auto 6 might sound like the least useful skill that Jason and Lucia would need to achieve their goals. As you progress through the game, you unlock different tools to help you deal with enemies and invade locations. However, none of the fancy technology you may have will work as well as a simple whistle in certain situations.

item.title: Dropout’s Most Unhinged Show Officially Returns with New Trailer
item.dc:creator: Austin Manchester
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV renewal/season announcement for non-horror series.] Dropout released a new trailer for the Vic Michaelis-led improvised talk show Very Important People, and season 4 premieres in December.
item.content:encoded: Fresh off their hilarious role in Star Wars Zero Company, Vic Michaelis returns to Dropout with a new season of Very Important People. Season 4 premieres next month, and Dropout released a new trailer on Wednesday that showcases just how chaotic it will get.

item.title: GTA 6 Fans Are Hissing Mad About Dolores the Snake
item.dc:creator: Jen Glennon
item.description: [Filtered: Reddit culture piece about minor game detail, not substantive news.] A Reddit post highlighting the inaccuracies of the reptile habitat in GTA 6 has captured the attention of gamers and normies alike
item.content:encoded: After more than a decade of waiting, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here. Perhaps most surprising of all, it's actually living up to the world's sky-high expectations, and players everywhere are sharing their delight and awe at the game's immaculate attention to detail on social media. But there's one group of players who aren't so thrilled about the level of realism in GTA 6: snake owners.

item.title: 10 Funniest ‘Far Side’ Comics About Mailmen and Dogs
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Generic nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip.] One of Gary Larson’s best running jokes in The Far Side was his many comics about mailmen and dogs. Here are the 10 best.
item.content:encoded: Dogs and mailmen are natural enemies that have been locked in battle for eons. The dogs view the mailmen as unwelcome invaders of their territory. Meanwhile, the mailmen view the dogs as vicious beasts preventing them from upholding their noble postal worker’s oath. It’s nearly as old as the struggle between good and evil — and just as epic.

item.title: Forget 'Blade Runner 2099,' Ridley Scott's Sci-Fi Survival Masterpiece Is Already on Streaming
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming clickbait: "is already on streaming" type article.] Ridley Scott’s 205 sci-fi film The Martian is the perfect way to prep for Blade Runner 2099
item.content:encoded: The long-awaited Blade Runner2099 arrives on Prime Video tonight at 9 p.m. Eastern time, which, frankly, feels a bit late at night to drop eight episodes the night before a major holiday. Executive produced by original Blade Runner director Ridley Scott, the sequel series takes place in a future Los Angeles where the replicants have taken over and demoted humans to second-class citizens. It’s the kind of show that looks like it deserves a dedicated, fully alert, all-day binge session, not to be drowsily cut short so you can wake up early enough to begin preparing the stuffing tomorrow.

item.title: 7 Funniest MST3K Episodes to Watch For Your Personal Turkey Day Marathon
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Generic list of old TV episode recommendations, not substantive news.] It's 14 straight hours and it's called Turkey Day
item.content:encoded: Mystery Science Theater 3000 fans have always had a special relationship with American Thanksgiving. The show originally premiered on Thanksgiving Day in 1988, back in its public access era on KTMA TV in Minneapolis. Three years later, Comedy Central ran the first "Turkey Day" MST3K marathon, as both an anniversary celebration for the show and a 30-hour Thanksgiving special.

item.title: How to flip your car in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Flipping your car in GTA 6 works differently from previous games. Here's how to flip your car so you don't have to pay Scooter Bros for delivery
item.content:encoded: Flipping your car in Grand Theft Auto 6 works a bit differently than it did in previous games. In Rockstar's bid for realism, the team made it so you can't flip your car while you're still in it. Instead, whichever character you're controlling will have to get out of the car and turn it over. Note that flipping only works on certain vehicles, though. You can flip cars, boats, even larger construction vehicles, but not planes.

item.title: Vice City portal Easter egg location in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Paulo Kawanishi
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's how to start and complete the Vice City portal easter egg in GTA 6 and the rewards you receive from it.
item.content:encoded: The Vice City portal Easter egg is a unique event in Grand Theft Auto 6 that lets you travel through time. It might not look like it, but the existence of a secret portal in Leonida is quite plausible, considering the UFOs appearing in the skies and the forgotten haunted hotels you can visit.

item.title: How to get your car out of the impound in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Paulo Kawanishi
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] In this guide, you learn how to get your car out of the police impound in GTA 6
item.content:encoded: It doesn't take long for one of your cars to end up at the police impound in Grand Theft Auto 6. You might have abandoned it near a crime scene, or they arrested you while you were driving it. While the circumstances may vary, you have only two ways to proceed if a car is impounded: you forget about it or you retrieve it.

item.title: Best way to reveal the map in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Johnny Yu
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Revealing the GTA 6 map takes a very long time. Here's the best method to remove the fog, so you can see the entire map and everything it has to offer
item.content:encoded: Revealing your map in Grand Theft Auto 6 is no easy task, as the map is huge. Defogging the map isn't necessary to complete the game, but it's nice to see what each area has to offer. By uncovering it, you can see every clothing store, gas station, Pay 'N' Spray, and more.

item.title: Amazon Confirms Rings of Power Season 4's Status Ahead of Season 3 Finale
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.category: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV series renewal announcement, not prestige/anticipated enough.] Amazon has officially announced Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power has been renewed for a fourth season
item.content:encoded: The third season of Rings of Power, Amazon's Lord of the Rings series on Prime Video, is set to conclude on Tuesday, Nov. 24 with the release of its final two episodes. That is, of course, if you didn't catch the seventh episode early in theaters. Before the credits roll, Amazon has revealed that fans will be getting more of Rings of Power soon as the show has been renewed for a fourth season.

item.title: Disney’s Unwatchable New Fantasy Movie is a Sloppy Harry Potter-The Incredibles Mash-Up
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Generic animated film review; lacks prestige or genuine anticipation.] Hexed is packed with nods to better stories
item.content:encoded: Hexed kicks off with a standard exposition dump explaining that Hexe was formed as a sanctuary for persecuted witches and wizards. Their realm is protected by a magical spell meant to be empowered through a ritual that the extra-special “chosen witch” will complete during an upcoming lunar event. Billie Doe (Hailee Steinfeld) opened a portal to Hexe when she was a baby, and her overprotective mom Alice (Rashida Jones) has been suppressing her daughter’s powers ever since. But when Billie accidentally regains her abilities and travels to Hexe, she runs afoul of its villainous ruler Queen Celeste (Jodie Foster).

item.title: Pokémon Go 'Twilight Wishes' event guide
item.dc:creator: Julia Lee
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's everything you need to know about Pokémon Go's "Twilight Wishes" event, including how to get the sun and moon crown Pikachu.
item.content:encoded: Pokémon Go’s "Twilight Wishes" event is here to wrap up the "Twilight Trails" season. Running from Nov. 24-30, this event brings back the Pokémon featured in the previous events throughout the season, and marks the return of Espeon and Umbreon in their themed scarfs, as well as Pikachu in their sun and moon crowns.

item.title: Pokémon’s Hyped Countdown Might Be Leading to a Letdown
item.dc:creator: Austin Manchester
item.description: [Filtered: Pokémon non-game news; music video announcement lacks substance.] Pokémon's social media has counting down toward something happening on Nov. 30, and it looks like the announcement will just be a music video.
item.content:encoded: In October and early November, The Pokémon Company started counting down toward the end of the month, as noted by Serebii webmaster Joe Merrick. Using Poké Ball-themed logos created for the franchise's 30th anniversary, Pokémon teased some sort of announcement for Nov. 30 at 14:00 UTC.

item.title: Avengers: Doomsday Officially Skips Awards Screenings to Avoid Spoiler Leaks
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: [Filtered: Big-franchise Marvel churn; casting/set gossip tier content.] Marvel’s Avengers: Doomsday is skipping the BAFTAs and Golden Globes to preserve spoilers ahead of release
item.content:encoded: Don't expect to see Avengers: Doomsday show up on the nomination lists at some of Hollywood's biggest awards shows in the coming months. That's because Disney and Marvel are taking extreme precautions to protect the intimate details of their upcoming superhero blockbuster, going so far as to withhold screeners in hopes of avoiding plot leaks. Still, this strategy won't dash all of Doomsday's award hopes.

item.title: James Cameron’s Sci-Fi Sequel Masterpiece Is Officially Being Removed from Netflix
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming departure notice; James Cameron prestige doesn't override this format.] James Cameron’s 1986 film Aliens is about to leave Netflix. Watch is and relive the epicfinal battle with the alien queen
item.content:encoded: In an action movie, there’s nothing worse than an underwhelming final battle. While Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings was one of the best post-Avengers: Endgame movies of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, its final battle became a disconnected CGI fest that was hard to follow. For Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Secret of the Ooze, the sequel’s fun energy was undermined when a mutated Shredder died after collapsing a dock onto himself without a fight ever even starting.

item.title: 25 Years Later, GTA 3 Is Still the Most Fascinating Open-World Experiment
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective; '25 years later' format is tossable filler.] Rockstar's 2001 GTA 3 changed the open-world game forever with its urban playground of Liberty City.
item.content:encoded: The artwork’s nothing to write home about, just a collage of pictures in red, blue, and green hues, featuring obscure faces, a police chopper, and a car up in flames. Your instinct is to just go with your gut; Silent Hill 2 is what you came here for, after all. But something’s telling you otherwise. Maybe it’s the store clerk going on about its open-world premise, or the name itself that strikes a chord within you. Whatever reason incites it, you make the ultimate decision. Little did you know, you’d be walking home with one of the greatest achievements in video game history.

item.title: Where to find the Port Gellhorn serial killer in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Finding Gelhorn's missing tourists in GTA 6 takes requires some careful sleuthing, but if you need help, here's where to look for the missing tourists
item.content:encoded: Finding Port Gelhorn's missing tourists and the serial killer in Grand Theft Auto 6 takes you on a twisted journey around the town, one with few guideposts and a lot of chances to get stuck. It's a macabre scavenger hunt with only a few pictures and knowledge of the surrounding area to go by, though the reward at the end is comparatively small. This is a quest where the storytelling, more than anything else, is the reward.

item.title: Every Playable Video Game in GTA 6, Ranked Worst to Best
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: [Filtered: Ranking/list article; similar to tier lists, not substantive analysis.] Grand Theft Auto 6 features four playable video games within the game. Here's how they stack up.
item.content:encoded: Grand Theft Auto 6 is so big that it’s actually five games in one. Like previous games in the series, there are several games-within-the-game that you can play while hanging out in Leonida. These aren’t just quick arcade games that you can play for a few minutes, but full-on console games that are actually pretty fun in their own right.

item.title: 'Dealer's Choice' mission choices and outcomes in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Marloes Valentina Stella
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] 'Dealer's Choice' is a mission in GTA 6 that makes you choose between pure or cut substances. Here are the 'Dealer's Choice' outcomes explained.
item.content:encoded: Choosing between pure or cut drugs in Grand Theft Auto 6 is tough; on the one hand, it'll be nice to make extra money… But on the other hand, shady dealings often end in shootouts. More than other GTA 6 missions, the "Dealer's Choice" mission in Chapter 3 has a "best" and a "worst" way to handle things.

item.title: Where to find the Silent Hill hotel in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Paulo Kawanishi
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's where to find the Silent Hill hotel in GTA 6, and how to open the safe inside the haunted Marbelle Hotel
item.content:encoded: The Silent Hill hotel is one of the secrets you can stumble upon in Grand Theft Auto 6. Like the meeting with Dave and Beelzebub, you can miss the chance to enter this specific hotel and experience the creepy event that takes place inside. From the outside, it looks like a regular building, but after you visit this place, Leonida will literally change for a while. Besides, there's a safe waiting for you to open and a unique reward to collect.

item.title: Naruto Movie Officially Casts Fan-favorite Actor for Key Role
item.dc:creator: Austin Manchester
item.description: [Filtered: Naruto anime adaptation casting news; anime excluded from interests.] Hiroyuki Sanada has been cast in the live-action Naruto movie from Spider-Man: Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton.
item.content:encoded: Spider-Man: Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton is gearing up for his next live-action adaptation of an iconic franchise. He's writing and directing a live-action Naruto movie, and is in the process of casting an important role.

item.title: Where to find the UFO dream house in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Ford James
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] This guide explains where to find the house that is depicted on planet Earth during the UFO dream sequence in GTA 6.
item.content:encoded: If you're looking for the UFO dream house location in Grand Theft Auto 6, that means you've already seen the UFO itself once. This unmarked optional mission begins when you investigate an abandoned car at the side of the road, follow a trail of clothes strewn on the floor, then discover a woman in a rather unfortunate situation, being beamed up into the sky. The next time you go to sleep, a concerning dream sequence happens, with one part of it showing somewhere in Leonida depicted onto what is supposed to be planet Earth.

item.title: Should you give the statue to Benedict Halifax during 'Dubious Provenance' in GTA 6?
item.dc:creator: Marloes Valentina Stella
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's what happens if you give or withhold the statue from Benedict Halifax in GTA 6, as well as how to deal with him later on in the mission.
item.content:encoded: Giving the statue to Halifax during the Grand Theft Auto 6 "Dubious Provenance" mission may not seem like the wisest choice, but don't be too quick to decide. In this GTA 6 mission, one choice is more rewarding and more time-efficient than the other.

item.title: 32 Years Later, The Best 'Peanuts' Rerun Comic Strip Is Still an All-Time Classic
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip, matches toss pattern.] He just got here and he's already confused
item.content:encoded: Every comic strip has an evolutionary arc. Every cartoonist changes their style over time as they hone their craft, develop their sense of humor shifts, master their particular style, and/or pander to their audience. Sometimes an early character may all but disappear from the comic, or some incidental member of the cast may take up the spotlight. It's part of the fun of going on archive binges, whether it's old newspaper comics or long-running web series. Comics are living things, and few of them stay in the places where they started.

item.title: Robert Pattinson's Forgotten Dark Fantasy Thriller Proves He's a Perfect James Bond
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Generic film recommendation lacking real substance; not horror.] The Lighthouse, which is available on HBO Max, is the perfect film for the Robert Pattinson skeptic
item.content:encoded: Not everybody is convinced Robert Pattinson is the right choice to be the next James Bond. Some are complaining Bond should be played by someone less famous, like he has in the past. Others feel he’s not masculine enough, or good-looking enough, or charismatic enough. Most of all, though, it seems many people don't love the idea that “the Twilight guy” is playing Bond.

item.title: 34 Years Later, the Best 'Far Side' Quote Will Still Leave You Speechless
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip, matches toss pattern.] Gary Larson's comic strip The Far Side was known for its visual humor, but this is the best-ever quote from the series
item.content:encoded: Larson didn’t do deep and inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful. Larson’s work was brilliant, and it sometimes took a few minutes to figure out what the punchline was. Take, this comic strip where an artist is painting a woman as a half-fly creature, for example. You likely see the woman or the painting first, and you wonder why the artist is painting her that way. Only after inspecting the comic more closely do you see the dead fly stuck to his glasses.

item.title: Star Wars Is Getting an Official IMAX 70mm Release for the First Time
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.description: [Filtered: Star Wars big-franchise churn; theatrical rerelease is filler.] In 2027, the original untouched Star Wars will return to movie theaters — and in IMAX 70mm screenings for the first time, Lucasfilm confirms.
item.content:encoded: Han will shoot first in 70 mm IMAX when the original Star Wars returns to movie theaters next year. Lucasfilm and IMAX have confirmed that the 50th anniversary rerelease of Star Wars will be on the biggest screens possible next February, giving fans a strong reason to return to theaters.

item.title: GTA 6 Is Getting Review Bombed in Zelda vs. GTA Troll War
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: [Filtered: Fan drama and culture war clickbait, not substantive game news.] Grand Theft Auto 6 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time fans are fighting over Metacritic scores as part of a larger anti-woke culture war.
item.content:encoded: Grand Theft Auto 6 may be the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic, and may have earned a record-breaking $3.79 billion on launch day, but that doesn't mean Rockstar Games' new blockbuster can't have its haters. Multiple groups have descended on GTA 6's Metacritic page to attack the game for its perceived shortcomings, much of that criticism is based on culture war nonsense.

item.title: Netflix’s (Very) R-Rated 45-Episode Sci-Fi Anthology Doesn’t Get the Attention It Deserves
item.dc:creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
item.description: [Filtered: Generic streaming recommendation, not prestige project or horror.] This genre-blend anthology boasts exceptionally well-crafted episodes.
item.content:encoded: Almost four decades after the film’s release, filmmakers David Fincher and Tim Miller attempted to reboot Heavy Metal, which eventually morphed into the Netflix sci-fi anthology, Love, Death & Robots. Although the series inevitably carries the DNA of Heavy Metal and its contemporaries, Love, Death & Robots carves out its distinct identity over 45 exceptional episodes. While sci-fi is at the heart of these anthology tales, the show blends everything from horror to comedy to complement the bountiful art styles that are a celebration of animation as a medium.
